text:
Sam H: Heads-up — AcmePipelines redlined the quote. They removed our price-protection clause, added a 12-month MFN-ish clause, and put a strict cap on pass-through overages. We already offered a 30% POC discount. Need quick pricing + legal guidance and next steps for deal desk.
Alice G: Context: POC starts next week. If it converts, expected ARR ~ $120k first year. We gave 30% to land the pilot; customer is pushing MFN back into the commercial terms.
Michael P: MFN + no price protection is risky. MFN as a broad promise prevents us from using future promos or targeted offers. Also keeps discount anchored for the term. Deal desk will want quantification.
Jessica (legal): Agree - the MFN language looks overly broad. Recommend narrowing scope: apply only to identical product SKUs and exclude future volume-based, channel, or targeted promotional pricing. Also suggest adding a limited price-protection window (e.g., 90 days) instead of removing it entirely. I can propose replacement wording.
Sam H: Can we accept a narrower MFN (industry-specific or sku-limited) if we add a 90-day protection and a cap on the MFN's applicability?
Michael P: Financial quick take (very rough):
```
List ARR baseline: $100,000
Offered POC discount: 30% -> customer pays $70,000 (delta $30k)
If MFN applies and customer expands to $300k, we'd be stuck at the $70k pricing unless carveouts exist. Foregone upside could be large.
```
Michael P: Bottom line: need Deal Desk + Legal + Finance to sign off on any MFN or broad protections. Also propose a true-up mechanism.
Jessica (legal): Proposed clause (suggested, narrow):
```
"Customer shall be entitled to the most favorable pricing that Vendor extends to other customers for the same product SKU and substantially similar terms within 12 months of the Effective Date, provided that (i) pricing extended pursuant to promotional campaigns, public offers, channel/partner discounts, or volume-based rebates are excluded, and (ii) Customer's price shall be subject to a 90-day price protection following execution. Any MFN claim must be submitted in writing and is limited to direct list pricing adjustments only."
```
Jessica (legal): That keeps MFN narrow, preserves promos/partner pricing, and caps protection window.
DealDesk Bot: New deal desk request form: https://redwood.internal/deal-desk/new — use template "pricing-exceptions" and include redline PDF.
Michael P: Approval flow I recommend:
  1) Finance: net revenue impact & IRR check
  2) Legal: clause scope sign-off
  3) Deal Desk (Director): commercial exception
Also require a committed-spend gate: e.g., discount only if 12-month committed spend >= $200k.
Alice G: I'll open the deal desk ticket and attach the redline + the POC forecast. Requesting conditional approval: 30% POC discount if commit >= $200k, MFN narrowed per legal text, and price protection limited to 90 days.
DealDesk Bot: Ticket created: DD-4521 — https://redwood.internal/deal-desk/tickets/DD-4521 (status: awaiting finance calc)
Michael P: Finance needs the ARR projection and expansion assumptions. Sam, can you add a month-by-month expected run-rate in the ticket so we can do the IRR/PSR? Also list any other customers in same vertical that might trigger comparability checks.
Sam H: Will add month-by-month numbers and comps in DD-4521 by EOD. Also attaching the customer's redline.
Alice G: Thanks everyone — once finance posts the calc we can route to legal for final wording and then to Deal Desk director. :thumbsup:
Sam H: Thanks — I'll follow up in the ticket.
